 Judgment

The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.2886/2006 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Ernakulam, is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 15.03.2005.

According to the petitioner, on 15.03.2005, while he was driving his car through Edakochi- Thoppumpadi road from south to north, a bus driven by the 2 nd respondent, in a rash and negligent manner dashed against his car.
As a result of which, he sustained injuries.
The 1st respondent is the owner of bus and the 3rd respondent is the insurer of the car.
According to the him, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
3. The 3rd respondent/insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy and disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It was further contended that the accident occurred MACA NO. 2949 OF 2014 2025:KER:11432 due to the negligence of the petitioner.
4. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A7, and Exts.X1 and X2.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
5. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,88,979/-.
6. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

7. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

8. Heard Sri.Rahul Sasi, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Sri.Alex Antony Sebastian, learned Standing Counsel appearing for the KSRTC and Sri.Dinesh Murickan, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company.
9.
In the accident the petitioner sustained a small punctured wound on the middle of right upper eye lid pearcing the eyelid - No vision to the right eye sight perception.
He was treated as inpatient for 7 days.

sentences.text: As per Ext.X1(a) certificate issued by the State Medical MACA NO. 2949 OF 2014 2025:KER:11432 Board, the permanent physical disability of the petitioner was assessed as 30%.
The learned counsel for the petitioner would argue that though the permanent physical disability as per Ext.X1(a) is only 30%, the functional disability of the petitioner is much more.
However, it is to be noted that in the accident, the petitioner lost eyesight of only one of his eyes, and he claims that he is a cable operator by profession.
Therefore, I do not find any grounds to interfere with the permanent physical disability of the petitioner as assessed by the State Medical Board and as accepted by the Tribunal.
11. In the claim petition the petitioner claimed the monthly income of Rs.6,000/-.
However, the Tribunal found that his monthly income is only Rs.4,000/-.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie during the year 2005, will come to Rs.5,000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the notional income of the petitioner is fixed at Rs.5,000/-.
12. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 43 years.

Therefore, 25% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 14, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

sentences.text:
In MACA NO. 2949 OF 2014 2025:KER:11432 the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.3,15,000/.
13.
Towards loss of earnings, the Tribunal has awarded only Rs.12,000/- being the monthly income for a period of 3 months.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the fact that he lost eyesight of right eye and he was treated as an inpatient for a period of 7 days, I hold that towards loss of earnings, he is entitled to get the monthly income for a period of 5 months, which will come to Rs.25,000/- (5,000 x 5).
14.
Towards the head extra nourishment, the Tribunal has not awarded any amount.
Towards pain and sufferings Rs.25,000/- was awarded.

Considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, I hold that towards pain and suffering, he is entitled to get a sum of Rs.35,000/- and towards extra nourishment he is entitled to get Rs.3,000/-.

15. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
16.
Therefore, the petitioner/ appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.4,42,779/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.
